text:
anna: FYI -- after the kernel selector change on canary, Mixtral MoE p99 jumped ~18% and we're seeing a lot more expert evictions. starting triage.
mike: any profiler output or flamegraph links?
anna: pasting a short profiler snapshot from the canary run:
```
perf_summary: tokens/sec=11.2, p50=42ms, p95=210ms, p99=460ms
router: avg_calls=720/s, topk=8, temp=1.0
expert_evictions: 12.4% -> baseline 1.1%
kv_hit_ratio: 0.58 -> baseline 0.86
kernel: selected=fast_mha_v2 (quant-path)
```
dave: that kv_hit_ratio drop screams cache churn. router is probably bouncing lots of contexts. did the kernel change alter batch sizes or scheduling?
anna: kernel selection bumped per-token batch packing threshold (we now favor the quant path for seq_len<=256). observed median batch size down from 8->5.
sree: smaller batches + more frequent context switches -> more KV pages evicted and rehydrated. also topk=8 increases routing skew, more hot experts.
mike: interesting. two axes: reduce routing pressure (lower topk or clamp routings), or increase memory locality (bigger batches / retain KV longer). quick experiments?
anna: spun a dev canary with router.temp=0.7 and topk=4. results after 10m:
```
perf_summary: tokens/sec=12.0, p50=40ms, p95=180ms, p99=320ms
kv_hit_ratio: 0.72
expert_evictions: 4.3%
notes: throughput slightly up, p99 improved but still ~12% reg vs baseline
```
dave: promising. lowering temp reduces entropy in router logits -> more deterministic routing. but risk of overloading top experts; topk clamp to 4 helps.
mike: alternative: bump expert parallelism on hot experts from 2->4 to absorb load. cost tradeoff though.
anna: tried parallelism bump on one shard (expert_pool.parallelism=4) + temp=0.8, topk=6:
```
perf_summary: tokens/sec=11.6, p50=41ms, p95=170ms, p99=290ms
kv_hit_ratio: 0.69
expert_evictions: 2.1%
cpu/gpu_util: gpu core steady, memory traffic up ~9%
```
sree: lower evictions is good. memory traffic increase aligns with more concurrent expert state use. still want to get kv_hit_ratio closer to 0.85.
mike: can we tune KV retention policy? maybe increase retention window or bump cache size per expert to reduce churn.
anna: quick test: kv_cache.retention_ms=120000 on canary (was 30000). short run (5m) shows kv_hit_ratio -> 0.81, p99 down to 250ms but token/sec slightly down due to memory pressure.
dave: memory pressure might trigger GPU allocations that slow kernels. we should profile memory alloc patterns.
mike: another angle: kernel choice. fast_mha_v2 favors small seqs but seems to reduce batching; maybe fallback to stable_mha for mixed seq workload. try dynamic kernel heuristic: if median batch size<6, prefer stable_mha.
anna: re-ran with dynamic kernel heuristic + temp=0.7 + topk=4. results:
```
perf_summary: tokens/sec=12.3, p50=38ms, p95=160ms, p99=220ms
kv_hit_ratio: 0.84
expert_evictions: 0.9%
notes: matches baseline latencies, throughput up slightly
```
deploy-bot: rolled kernel-selector patch to canary at ts=1956789050 (commit: 0a9f3d)
anna: post-deploy observation: p99 back to baseline, eviction down. leaving the canary running for 2h to watch for regression.
sree: capture traces for a few hot requests and attach kernel timelines. want to check RoPE scaling impact too — we saw slight logit variance when we changed quant kernels earlier.
mike: good call. RoPE scaling + routing can amplify head imbalance. add a small eval to check output divergence across kernel choices.
anna: created follow-up issue and perf job: https://rwl-internal/issue/INF-4821. next steps: (1) run longer canary for 2h, (2) try per-expert parallelism auto-scale heuristic, (3) tighten kernel selection thresholds, (4) add RoPE/regression eval. will post updates.
mike: thanks for the triage. if canary holds, we should push selector rollback + the new heuristic to prod next week.
anna: ack. ping me if you want access to canary logs or to run extra experiments. :thumbsup:
